relationships.description: The component creates, reads, updates or deletes instances of the data structure while performing its behaviour, so the data object is part of the state it handles.
relationships.evidence: The component's class or module instantiates, deserializes, mutates or returns the data object's type, for example as a repository method parameter or return type.

relationships.description: The component performs operations on the protected resource at runtime, which makes it a subject whose actions on that resource are checked by access control.
relationships.evidence: The component's code calls the resource's protected operations, such as a guarded API path, table or file, or the security configuration lists the component's service identity as a principal on that resource.

relationships.description: The component is the active element responsible for executing the internal function, so the function's work is carried out by this component and by no other.
relationships.evidence: The methods implementing the function are defined on the component's class or within its module and are invoked only from inside the component's deployment unit.

relationships.description: The component is the active element behind the access point, handling every request that arrives through that controller, endpoint or listener.
relationships.evidence: The controller, gRPC binding or message listener is registered in the component's bootstrap or routing configuration and delegates directly to the component's handlers.

relationships.description: The function is an integral part of the component and is not defined, deployed or meaningful outside it, so removing the component removes the function.
relationships.evidence: The function's code lives only within the component's package or source tree and is not exported or reused by any other deployable unit.

relationships.description: The component's permitted operations and data access are limited by the rules of the security policy, so its behaviour must stay within what the policy allows.
relationships.evidence: The policy's target selectors name the component or its endpoints, or the component's middleware or policy-engine configuration loads and evaluates that policy before acting.

relationships.description: The component contains the working code of the security control, turning the documented countermeasure into executing behaviour.
relationships.evidence: The component's source contains the control logic, such as input sanitization, rate limiting, encryption or token validation, and the countermeasure record points to that module as its implementation.

relationships.description: The component's behaviour lowers the likelihood or impact of the identified threat, reducing the residual risk recorded against it.
relationships.evidence: The threat model or risk register lists the component as a mitigating element for the threat, backed by code that blocks or detects the attack vector.

relationships.description: The component offers the access point to users or other components, making its services reachable through that controller, endpoint or channel.
relationships.evidence: The component's codebase declares and exposes the interface, for example by mounting the route, publishing the gRPC service definition or subscribing the listener at startup.

relationships.description: The component's internal behaviour is what concretely delivers the operations that the service promises to its consumers.
relationships.evidence: The component's class implements the service's interface or contract, such as an OpenAPI or protobuf service definition, with method bodies backing each operation.

relationships.description: The component is the automated system that concretely delivers the business service to its customers or stakeholders.
relationships.evidence: Architecture documentation or a service catalog maps the business service to the component, and the component's operations carry out the service's core transactions.

relationships.description: The component supplies the concrete implementation that gives the product the stated ability.
relationships.evidence: A capability map or product documentation links the capability to the component, and the component's code implements the behaviour the capability describes.

relationships.description: The component implements the user-visible functionality that makes up the feature, so shipping the component delivers the feature.
relationships.evidence: The feature's tickets, feature flag or release notes reference changes in the component's repository, and the component's code contains the feature's logic.

relationships.description: Building and operating the component directly brings about the desired end state that the goal expresses.
relationships.evidence: Architecture decision records or roadmap documents cite the component as the delivery vehicle for the goal, with metrics attributing goal progress to it.

relationships.description: The component's design is a concrete embodiment of the architectural principle, demonstrating how that principle is applied in practice.
relationships.evidence: An architecture decision record or design document for the component explicitly cites the principle, and its structure reflects it, for example statelessness or API-first design.

relationships.description: The component meets the stated need, so the requirement is considered fulfilled by its delivered behaviour or qualities.
relationships.evidence: A traceability matrix links the requirement ID to the component, and acceptance tests for that requirement pass against the component.

relationships.description: The component supports the people holding the business role in carrying out their responsibilities, acting as a tool they rely on.
relationships.evidence: The component's role-based access configuration or user documentation grants the business role access to screens or operations designed for its tasks.

relationships.description: The source component relies on the target component's functionality at runtime, so the target is a dependency the source needs to do its work.
relationships.evidence: The source component injects, imports or calls the target, for example through a dependency-injection binding, package dependency or HTTP/gRPC client configured with the target's address.

notes: assigned-to and composes toward ApplicationFunction overlap; composition between active structure and behaviour is not valid ArchiMate. assigned-to and provides toward ApplicationInterface are redundant; ArchiMate uses composition for component-to-interface. Realizing Goal and Principle directly is questionable, since core elements normally realize Requirements, which in turn realize goals and principles.
